chunks: 4798 - And al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The waiting period ('iddah) of a woman who does not menstruate, a mustahadah who does not become pure, and a young girl who has despaired [of menstruation] is three months; and the waiting period of one whose menstruation is regular is three menstrual cycles.

key_terms.أَشْهُرٍ: months, used here as the measure of the waiting period
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman subject to the legal ruling
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: a woman experiencing irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.حِيَضٍ: menstrual cycles counted for the waiting period
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: the legally prescribed waiting period after divorce

ai.seo_question: What is the 'iddah for a woman who does not menstruate or whose bleeding is irregular in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the 'iddah of different categories of women after divorce. It distinguishes between women whose menstruation is absent or irregular, whose waiting period is three months, and women with regular menstruation, whose waiting period is three menstrual cycles.
